proof.title: Nothing leaves this tab. Go and check.
proof.lead: Every site that asks you to upload a PDF also promises not to look at it. This one makes a duller promise: it never receives the file, so there is nothing to look at. You can check that in about a minute.

engine.title: It runs on your machine
engine.body: PDFium, compiled to WebAssembly, renders pages in a Web Worker. pdf-lib reads and writes the file structure in the page itself. Either way the bytes go from your disk into your own memory and back out as a download.

network.title: Watch the Network tab
network.body: Open developer tools, switch to Network, then run any tool on any file. The request count does not move. The page is served with a Content-Security-Policy that blocks outbound connections anyway.

offline.title: Then pull the plug
offline.body: Turn the network off and reload. Tools you have already opened keep working, because they were never running anywhere else. A site that uploads cannot survive that test.

privacy.title: Privacy, without the fine print
privacy.lead: There is no policy to read here, because there is no data to have a policy about. Nothing you open in fuckpdf is sent anywhere, and there is nowhere for it to be sent.

what.title: What happens to your file
what.body: You choose a file. Your browser reads it into memory and hands the bytes to an engine: PDFium, compiled to WebAssembly, in a Web Worker, or pdf-lib in the page itself. The engine produces a new file and the download comes from a blob in this tab. No step in that list touches a network.

verify.title: How to check
verify.body: Open your browser's developer tools, go to the Network tab, and run a tool. Nothing new appears. The site is served with a Content-Security-Policy of connect-src 'self', so the browser would refuse an outbound request even if the code tried to make one.

offline.title: Offline
offline.body: After the first load, tools you have already used keep working with no connection at all. Disconnect and try it. A site that processes files on a server cannot pass that test. That is what makes it worth running.

stored.title: What is stored
stored.body: One value in this browser's own localStorage: whether you picked the light or the dark theme. No cookies, no analytics, no telemetry, no error reporting, and no fonts or scripts loaded from anyone else.

about.title: A small tool for an annoying file format
about.lead: fuckpdf does the boring things people actually need to do to a PDF (merge it, split it, rotate it, number it, crop it) in the browser, immediately, for free.

why.title: Why it exists
why.body: The usual PDF sites take a file you probably should not hand to a stranger (a contract, a payslip, a scan of your passport), upload it to a machine you know nothing about, put you in a queue, and ask you to sign up somewhere around the third page. None of that is required to rotate a page. The work is arithmetic, and your computer does arithmetic.

how.title: How it works
how.body: Every tool is a pure step that takes bytes and returns bytes. Two engines do the work: PDFium, compiled to WebAssembly, for rendering pages, and pdf-lib for reading and writing the file structure. PDFium loads only when a tool needs it, in a Web Worker, so the interface stays responsive and nothing large downloads until it has to.

scope.title: What it will not do
scope.body: It will not edit existing text inside a PDF, recover a password you do not have, or run anything that needs a model or a server. Where a conversion loses fidelity, the tool says so before you run it instead of after.

licenses.title: Licenses
licenses.lead: This application is open source under the MIT licence, and it stands on a stack of other people's work. A complete dependency inventory is generated with each release build.

app.title: This application
app.body: MIT. The interface is built with React, React Router, Tailwind CSS, HeroUI, Zustand, i18next, dnd-kit and fflate, all MIT-licensed. Comlink is Apache-2.0 and the lucide icon set is ISC.

engines.title: PDF engines
engines.body: PDFium is BSD-3-Clause, and the WebAssembly build used here ships under MIT. pdf-lib is MIT. PDFium is loaded only by the tools that render pages, which is why the first page is small and the engine is not.

fonts.title: Fonts
fonts.body: Space Grotesk and JetBrains Mono, both under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, served from this origin. No font is fetched from a third party, because no request is made to one.
